item.title: Trying to...
item.content:encoded:
Bring attention back to this SCP. Because I have one main issue I'll be brief. I, personally, feel as though there sould be an SCP based on Foundation trivia. One of those cliches too good to leave out. So the comparison between this and 024 makes me feel like 263 is the play-at-home model people used to get as a participant on gameshows. XD

However this….

If during the forty-five seconds, […] the subject interacts with a computer greater than twenty-seven centimeters, SCP-263-1 will accuse the subject of cheating and the subject will combust in the same manner as described above.[…] Portable consumer electronic devices, such as mobile telephones, PDAs, and laptop computers smaller than twenty-seven centimeters do not cause the subject to combust, thus allowing the subject to find the information required to correctly answer the question within the provided time.

…whhhhhaaaaaa? Why? I don't know why but this bothers me. Does anyone know why this is? Did the original author use it as a panacea (?) so The Foundation could have a way to cheat and, therefore, efficiently experiment?

If it's not, I feel a mild descriptor (maybe just because the THOMAS is old tech?) as to why it doesn't notice computers 27 centimetres or less. Until then, I actually have to -1 this one.

Oh and maybe tweak the numerical representation to updated standards.

Portable consumer electronic devices, such as mobile telephones, PDAs, and laptop computers smaller than twenty-seven (27) centimeters.

But that might be old as well as nitpicky.

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
You know, SCP-1561 does reference Site-19 in it, but you are right that it is not contained there. Derp.

I do think you are right in that it should be all humanoids or all items, so lets see if we can get:

  • A Series II article
  • That is a humanoid
  • Located at site 19.

Such options include: SCP-1770, and SCP-1467 both of which could make for neat trophies included in the collection given by SCP-263 as a prize. Since I don't want to bog down with too many crosslinks, lets roll with SCP-1467 for now.

As such, recommending the following revision of the proposal:

  • A series of eight gold plated miniature statuettes resembling humanoid anomalies contained at Site-19, including SCP-2278, and SCP-1467. The statuettes are marked with the anomalies object number on the base, and do not appear otherwise anomalous. (value $17,315)

Alright, so we have this TV game show that has inherent knowledge about the facility its in, and it gives out prizes. Wouldn't an interesting prize, and a means of providing a crosslink or two, be if the prize was a collection of a few miniature statuettes of anomalies contained at Site-19. Recommending the inclusion of the following addition to the prize section:

  • A series of eight gold plated miniature statuettes resembling anomalies contained at Site-19, including SCP-2278, SCP-1561, and SCP-1687. The statuettes are marked with the anomalies object number on the base, and do not appear otherwise anomalous. (value $17,315)

Admittedly, the connection here is that all three of the above anomalies are contained at Site-19 according to their articles, and were chosen partially because they are Series II and Series III, but also because the object itself would make an interesting statuette.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: Re: CALL FOR REVIEW
item.content:encoded:
This is pretty poorly written; the biggest problem I have with this SCP though, was nailed back on page 1:

Surprised no has mentioned this one is actually SAFE. Unplug it and stick it in a box.

I see no compelling reason for further testing, and furthermore no compelling reason not to decommission it. There's nothing to suggest that testing is necessary for containment or that the 'prize' is worth risking researchers' lives over. Not to mention, the researchers require access to the entire Foundation database - which normally has strict compartmentalized access control based on Level, Classification / current assignments… is there a compelling reason to throw Information Security out the window or assign *Level 5* researchers to this thing?

The rewrite should address these weaknesses.

item.title: CALL FOR REVIEW
item.content:encoded:
This is a call for review for this article.

Let me tell you all a story. A long, long time ago, back in early 2009, a young wannabe writer was skimming through the SCP series, completely in awe of what these authors could accomplish with such limiting resources at their disposal. In his browsing, this young noob came across a weird SCP, one about this TV that played a broadcast of a game show called "Cash or Ash". This article was different from the others. It was charming, bizarrely fun, made you really believe you were an audience member of this gameshow of riches and horrors as hosted by a wonderfully over the top host.

If you haven't gathered by now, that noob was me. This article, Cash or Ash, this is what solidified my love of the SCP series. It showed me that horror wasn't always necessarily the primary draw of an article. Sometimes you could just enjoy an article because it was fun to read, or because the associated anomaly just came off as a hoot and a half. This article still sticks with me as one of my favorites, partly out of nostalgia but also mostly because of how believable it is for me from an in-universe perspective. I love game shows, and everything about this one, from the asking easy to fucking impossible questions to the absolute showmanship of how losing contestants "leave", all beautifully represented here.

In particular I like the host of the show. On the surface he just looks like your standard game show host, but when you look at some of the details the article has given about him, you get a sense there's something deeper to him. The fact that he takes personal offense to cheaters, or the fact that the only "cash" the show gives out has his smiling face on it, these facts suggest a greater degree of character to him than many current articles I've seen.

Unfortunately, even I can't deny that this article hasn't aged well. The tone is not nearly up to snuff from what we expect in this day and age, it's far too conversational and nonprofessional. In addition, the [DATA EXPUNGED] at the end of the article is just a lazy way to expunge a fact that I'm not altogether sure even exists.

Of course, you can't talk about the downsides of this article without talking about one of the biggest thorns for people, and that is its relation to the Foundation. Many people have criticized the fact that it dispenses facts specific to the Foundation, or the fact that it dispenses objects that have been classified as SCP objects. These are both valid complaints, and I feel that this article could be improved should these two facts are either expanded upon or reworked. For instance, if the trivia questions changed wherever the TV was, that would justify it's primary effect. On the flip side, if that were changed to just be facts about the world in general and information about the Foundation happened to be a part of it, that could also be a justification for its inclusion.

A few quotes about this SCP:

This SCP has always bothered me. It's basically a takeout version of SCP-024 that manufactures SCPish objects.

I feel that 024 did more with the concept, and did it better.

-pooryoric

I don't really mind the fiendish game show concept, but the SCP trivia I do. Flames that can't be extinguished and don't harm the environment? Mmmeh. I think I'd like it more if there weren't any visible flames, but the viewer would internally burn to ashes or something. And what's up with the random items? What does that have anything to do with cash? This is more "Flames or Random Items" than "Cash or Ash". Too inconsistent for my liking. Downvoted.

-ignotum per ignotius

Okay so I see everyone's problems with it and I agree, but I feel like this SCP could really be pulled through with the question page, possibly questions that help researchers conduct new experiments. Maybe even new SCP facts?

-Sine Nomine Nemo

Of course, these are just a handful of thoughts on the matter. I am formally asking any and all readers to look at this SCP and give some feedback on how it could be improved, how it could be altered so that it can become the fully realized idea that this wide-eyed former noob saw in this article those many years ago.

Arguably, if you lock it in a storage box and never turn it on, nothing bad will happen, right?

On the one hand, I might like to see it make something bad happen, e.g. it's a game show so it needs to run at least once a week or it will try to take over the next closest television set (CRT only, since it doesn't recognize new tech) that is turned on after a time threshhold. On the other hand, I'm given to understand that SCPs that make you use them are a bit of a cliche, so maybe it'd just be better to classify it as safe.
